chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Khuzaymah ibn Yaqtin, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Inheritance is received from the grandfathers: the father's father and the mother's father, and from the grandmothers: the father's mother and the mother's mother.
ai.seo_question: Which grandparents inherit from their grandchildren according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the scope of 'grandparents' (al-ajdad/al-ajdad) in Shia inheritance jurisprudence, confirming that all four grandparents—paternal and maternal on both sides—are eligible heirs. This ruling is significant as it resolves potential ambiguities regarding whether inheritance extends only to the direct paternal line or includes the maternal lineage, aligning with the principle of equal representation among ascendants when no closer relatives exist. The narration underscores the comprehensive nature of Shia fiqh in distributing shares among all qualifying ascendant ancestors.
